findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — [confidence 75][P2] `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> {` enumerates the typed all-clients resource while client-specific resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never receive a type, so getClientsWithPermission omits specifically granted client IDs and returns the resource-type name `Clients` for an all-clients grant instead of actual client IDs.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:224 — [confidence 75][P3][advisory] `Collection<Permission> permissions = root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server);` and the following scope scan are duplicated at lines 249 and 276, forcing future permission-result handling changes into three places and risking inconsistent list versus individual checks; although the entry points resolve different resources, that does not require duplicating evaluation, and delegating both hasPermission overloads to the existing hasGrantedPermission deletes two evaluation-and-scan blocks.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — [confidence 75][P1] `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) {` authorizes a caller with the all-Clients VIEW grant to read a client whose individual VIEW policy denies that caller, because canView() evaluates only the type resource and returns before the client policy is evaluated, bypassing the resource-specific restriction established by the existing all-users-plus-individual-denial semantics.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — [confidence 100, P2, advisory] `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), onlyMyAdminUserPolicy);` grants all three scopes simultaneously, so the test still passes when the two mapping checks are swapped or CONFIGURE incorrectly authorizes mappings, leaving delegated administrators exposed to undetected scope-boundary regressions; the strongest rebuttal is that before/after checks prove authorization works, but they never isolate which grant authorizes each operation.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:102 — [confidence 100, P2, advisory] `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE);` introduces client-scope role-mapping authorization without any corresponding grant/deny exercise in the changed FGAP tests, so a wrong scope constant or unconditional denial survives the suite and breaks administrators assigning role scope mappings; the strongest rebuttal is that other mapping tests exercise the shared permission evaluator, but those tests never invoke this distinct method or its REST integration.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
